newsitem.title: USA: Jailer says Whitewater prisoner too much trouble.
newsitem.headline: Jailer says Whitewater prisoner too much trouble.

text.p: The jailer of Whitewater defendant Susan McDougal said Friday that he wants her out of his jail almost as much as she does.
Faulkner County Sheriff Bob Blankenship said McDougal's celebrity is costing him too much money and time, so he has asked federal authorities to move her out.
"Things have got out of hand," he said.
Blankenship said McDougal is so sought after by the national media that he can no longer handle it.

"I'm tired of paying overtime. When the Today Show came to put her on live, they arrived at four in the morning. I have to bring in extra people to maintain security. The same for Fox and CBS and CNN and 'Geraldo,'" he said.

McDougal was sent to the Faulkner County jail in September on a contempt-of-court citation after she refused to cooperate with Whitewater investigators looking into the business affairs of President Clinton and first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton.

She and former husband James McDougal, who were once partners with the Clintons in the failed Whitewater real estate venture, were convicted in May of fraud and conspiracy for bilking federally-backed financial institutions in the mid-1980s. Susan McDougal still must serve a two-year sentence for those convictions.
James McDougal is cooperating with Starr's probe and remains free, pending sentencing.
Susan McDougal has tried to get out of jail for the contempt charge, but on Thursday a federal judge denied her request that it be thrown out.
She was sent to Faulkner County jail because the county has a contract with the U.S. Marshal's office to house federal prisoners.

Bob Leighton, chief deputy U.S. Marshal in Little Rock, said the federal government would attempt to accomodate Blankenship. "We've placed a request with the U.S. Bureau of Prisons that she be moved, but it may take a few days," he said.
In the meantime, Blankenship has restricted McDougal's press contacts to telephone interviews and has barred camera crews from his jail.
